transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-05 09:32 PST | 48m | Opal Retail Q4 operational burn & roadmap huddle
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jordan Ellis (Head of ML - Opal), Samantha Price (VP Eng), Ravi Mehta (DevOps), Alicia Tan (Product)

Summary (auto): Costs up in Oct due to increased inference per session; exploring small Dedicated commit + caching + quantization to reduce unit cost. Agreement to run pilot and exchange logs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok, hey everyone thanks for doing this. quick agenda — cost review, reliability, pilot and security Qs. Jordan you said you had the spend spike to show?
[00:24] Jordan Ellis: yeah so, uh, october was funky. we saw ~2.9x normal token volume for the recommendations path, partly A/B test misfire, partly real traffic. that pushed our monthly to, like, $78k which surprised finance.
[00:48] Samantha Price: and that was with caching turned on? we thought prefix caching was active for recs?
[01:06] Jordan Ellis: we had partial caching, but the KV cache wasn't used for a subset of signed-in flows. also prompt variance made batching less effective.
[01:28] Liam O'Connor: that makes sense — batching efficiency drop + cold cache will blow up per-token costs. for that traffic shape we usually recommend either a small Dedicated pool or more aggressive prefix caching and quantization.
[01:52] Ravi Mehta: quick question on Dedicated — does that lock us into specific gpus / regions? we have a SOC2 audit in Q1 so need region assurance.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Dedicated is region-aware, you can pin capacity to a region and we can do a VPC peering setup for Private-like isolation. SOC2 and audit logs are supported; we'll share the security pack.
[02:36] Speaker 1: (inaudible) are there penalties for bursting out of commit?
[02:45] Maya Chen: no hard penalty, burst is allowed but billed at a higher rate — so it's about economics not hard throttle.
[03:02] Jordan Ellis: when we modeled commit earlier the math assumed uniform usage; with spikes the unit economics were worse. if we do a small committed pool for the recs and keep chat on hosted, that could help.
[03:25] Samantha Price: also we wanted more granularity in the console — per-route token costs and per-model latency. current dashboards aggregate too much for our finance team.
[03:45] Liam O'Connor: noted. Console is being updated — we can add a per-route token breakdown and per-token cost column. I'll file that feature request and include sample screenshots.
[04:08] Alicia Tan: for roadmap alignment, we'll need to know when any model rollouts could disrupt p95. can Redwood do canary rollouts by customer route?
[04:25] Maya Chen: yes — Canary + automatic fallback to a cheaper variant is part of the rollout tooling. there's also eval gating so you can validate quality before full switch.
[04:45] Jordan Ellis: security — our InfoSec wants KMS integration and proof that customer KV cache isn't accessible cross-tenant. we also need longer audit log retention for six months.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: we support KMS/HSM integrations, and our tenant isolation for KV cache is strict. audit retention is configurable with an add-on — I'll attach the spec.
[05:28] Ravi Mehta: great. For pilot we'd like to run a 2-week dedicated benchmark with our top 50 prompts and traffic trace. how should we pass that data?
[05:45] Maya Chen: send logs via secure S3 link or share a scrubbed trace through the Dropbox link we'll provide. we'll treat it as test data.
[06:02] Jordan Ellis: side note, there was also a brief outage last month — 12m — during a scheduled rollout. Ops flagged that our fallback didn't trigger cleanly. what happened?
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: that was an edge-case with rollout policy not matching the route signature; we patched the policy handler. internal postmortem shows fix deployed, and we added a unit test. we can run a replay to show expected fallback behavior.
[06:45] Speaker 1: can you show the p99 numbers for the last month?
[06:52] Liam O'Connor: p99 for recs peaked at ~1.2s during the spike, p95 stayed under 450ms most of the time. I'll include the percentile charts in the bench doc.
[07:18] Samantha Price: cost controls — can we set hard caps and notify before spend hits thresholds? we need CFO-friendly alerts.
[07:32] Maya Chen: yes, quotas + alerting available. you can set account-level and route-level caps. notifications via email / webhook.
[07:48] Jordan Ellis: ok so immediate ask: give us three options — short burst pricing, small Dedicated commit with autoscale, and Private deployment estimate. include expected p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[08:07] Maya Chen: will do. we'll propose numbers through 90-day and 12-month lenses.
[08:18] Alicia Tan: about quantization — earlier you mentioned quantized variants might hit accuracy. what's the usual lift or delta in quality?
[08:33] Liam O'Connor: depends on model family. for our recommended open models, 4-bit quantization yields ~1-3% drop on naturalness for recommendation text, often acceptable. we'll do evals on your prompt set.
[08:55] Jordan Ellis: please run quality regressions tied to our prompts — we care about false negatives in product recs.
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: understood, we'll add targeted evals and a fail-gate for any model that drops below your threshold.
[09:20] Maya Chen: next — pilot timeline. propose: share logs by 11/12, Redwood runs bench 11/13-11/24, deliver results 11/25, decision meeting week of 11/27. good?
[09:38] Jordan Ellis: sounds tight but feasible. I'll try to accelerate the logs.
[09:46] Speaker 1: quick ops question on autoscale — does dedicated auto-scale have warm-up latency?
[09:55] Liam O'Connor: there's a short spin-up for new workers; autoscale can pre-warm based on predicted traffic patterns. for strict p95 targets we recommend a small baseline commit.
[10:15] Samantha Price: finance will want to know how quickly costs drop after we move to Dedicated. can you model the Feb-Mar seasonal ramp?
[10:29] Maya Chen: we can run that scenario if you share the forecast. include seasonality and A/B experiment flags.
[10:40] Jordan Ellis: we also had questions about model version pinning. We need the ability to pin specific model hashes per route during promos.
[10:53] Liam O'Connor: model pinning by version and canarying is supported. you can lock to a version until a manual release.
[11:06] Alicia Tan: any concerns with data residency if we go Dedicated in a different region?
[11:13] Maya Chen: we recommend aligning region to your data residency policies. Private offers the most control if strict rules apply.
[11:22] Jordan Ellis: procurement asked whether there are minimum terms for Dedicated.
[11:27] Maya Chen: minimums vary; small pilots have no long-term lock. Dedicated commit has quarterly or annual options; we'll outline both in the pricing doc.
[11:40] Speaker 1: is there a recommended caching strategy for recommendation results?
[11:48] Liam O'Connor: prefix caching on the user-session key and a TTL tuned to business metrics — we usually do short TTL (30-120s) for recs plus local LRU caching in the app for repeated impressions.
[12:05] Samantha Price: how about instrumentation to attribute tokens to product lines? billing needs that.
[12:14] Maya Chen: Console can surface per-route token counts; for internal product-level split you can add route tags and we'll export per-tag cost reports.
[12:28] Jordan Ellis: ok let's recap — Redwood: pricing scenarios + bench plan + security pack. Opal: logs + success criteria + internal approvers.
[12:40] Maya Chen: exactly. I'll send a succinct recap and a calendar invite for the bench kickoff.
[12:48] Speaker 1: one more small ask — can we get an export of last 90 days of per-route latency and cost?
[12:56] Liam O'Connor: yes I'll generate a CSV and upload to the secure link.
[13:05] Jordan Ellis: thanks all. quick note — we might spin a small config change to disable a noisy A/B test to reduce immediate burn. will confirm in the next 24 hours.
[13:18] Maya Chen: perfect. let's aim to reconvene after bench results.
[13:25] Meeting end: 48m

Notes about transcript quality: automatic transcription had a few mis-heard product names (Redwood Optimize sometimes 'Redwood Opti-mize') and a faint background in one attendee channel. Some speaker attributions generic.
